plan.notes: Source: official Le Moyne College 2023-2024 undergraduate catalog (PDF), 'Typical Program for Computer Science Major (B.S.)', catalog pp. 197-198; transcribed 2026-09-30 into ~/workspace/degree-wave2-work/d2-lemoyne/. TRUE degree name is 'Computer Science Major (B.S.)' (catalog heading). Catalog year 2023-2024: the 2024-2025 catalog PDF was unreachable (server timeout), so the newest accessible catalog was used. CREDIT TOTAL: the catalog's degree minimum is 120 credit hours ('Total Credit Hours 120' in the requirements table), but the published 'Typical Program' prints 'Total Credit Hours 126'; per the sequence-wins rule this plan uses the sequence's own total of 126 (17+17+17+16+16+15+13+15). TRANSCRIPTION NOTE: the catalog lays the typical program out in two side-by-side columns and the PDF text extraction interleaves them; Freshman Spring's five courses are CSC 185 (4), MTH 146 (4), EAC (3), HST 111 (3), PHL 110 (3) = 17, with 'PHL 110 Introduction to Philosophy 3' and its 'Credit Hours 17' line extracted at the top of p. 197; the eight printed semester totals sum exactly to the printed 126. A stray 'ENG 310 Literature and Culture 3 / Credit Hours 16' fragment extracted on p. 198 is extraction noise (ENG 310 is confirmed in the Junior Spring 15-credit semester). PREREQS are the catalog's stated course prerequisites. The catalog lists a 0-credit 'CSC 175L Lab' in the course descriptions, but the typical program does not list it separately, so it is not modeled as a slot. CSC electives: the catalog requires one project-based elective (CSC 441, CSC 445), one systems-based elective (CSC 411, CSC 425, CSC 480 & CSC 481), one theory-based elective (CSC 355, CSC 471), and two additional CSC courses numbered 300+ (not 499); the four 'CSC Elective' slots are student-choice with these options (known catalog prereqs: CSC 355 req. CSC 185; CSC 411 and CSC 425 req. CSC 276). Capstone: 'CS Capstone Experience' (3 cr; catalog lists CSC 490, CSC 496, CSC 498 as capstone experience courses; prerequisite: Senior Standing). EAC = Encountering Another Culture/Language; the catalog recommends world language at intermediate/advanced level (6 cr total). Natural Science = the 8-credit lab-based science sequence (4+4).
